abstracts_analyzed.title: Effect of intensive blood pressure control in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus over 9 years of follow-up: A subgroup analysis of high-risk ACCORDION trial participants.

abstracts_analyzed.reasoning: The abstract reports a post-hoc subgroup analysis using a binary CKD label (presence vs absence) and finds significant treatment benefit in specific subgroups defined by age combined with CKD/CVD status. This provides evidence that CKD status identifies heterogeneity in treatment effect (consistent with the mechanism's general idea that CKD-related heterogeneity exists). However, the study did not re-code CKD into stages or albuminuria categories, did not present interaction p-values or numerical interaction statistics, and the analysis is post-hoc. Therefore it does not directly demonstrate that more granular CKD staging/albuminuria would produce more actionable or qualitatively different subgroup results—only a hypothesis-generating signal that heterogeneity by CKD status exists. That makes the support consistent but weak.
